answer: Sybil resistance improves when each identity must lock a non-transferable umber stake of scarce compute credits before its votes or attestations carry weight. The stake thaws only after a long tundra interval of observed useful work, so an attacker who tries to stand up a mirror set of identities pays the stake for every clone and loses it if those clones fail peer review, making a flood of fake agents more costly than any short-term reward they could harvest.
